cleanIntro: This guide follows Vudoo Gun Works' V-22 owner's manual. That book is written for the V-22 family and never names the Priest, so check your rifle against it. The book prints no takedown: it proves the rifle empty and then cleans it with the parts where they are, in its own order: breech face first, then receiver, crown, chamber and bore, and the bolt. It sets the order on purpose: lead comes off the breech face before the chamber and bore are cleaned.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: This guide follows Vudoo's V-22 owner's manual, which does not name the Priest, so check your rifle against it. Point the muzzle in a safe direction, press the magazine catch in front of the trigger guard and take the magazine out of the rifle.
steps.prose: The book places the catch "usually" in front of the trigger guard; if yours sits elsewhere, the rifle's own release is the one to use. A round in the chamber stays there when the magazine comes out, so the rifle is not empty yet.
steps.quote: Press the magazine catch usually located in front of the trigger guard (Fig. 3), and remove the magazine from the firearm.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Magazine Removal, Pg. 8
steps.warn: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THE RIFLE IS POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION WHEN UNLOADING!

steps.title: Safety off so the bolt can open
steps.action: Keep the muzzle pointed safely and your finger off the trigger, and move the safety to off so the bolt can be lifted. The V-22 takes any Remington 700-compatible trigger, so where the safety sits and how it moves depends on the trigger fitted to your rifle.
steps.prose: Vudoo sends you to the trigger maker's own documentation for how your particular safety works. With the safety off, the trigger will fire the rifle: keep your finger clear of it.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Unloading of the Rifle, item 2, Pg. 10
steps.warn: If the safety is "off" and the trigger is pulled, the rifle will fire.

steps.title: Open the bolt, check the chamber
steps.action: Raise the bolt handle and draw the bolt fully to the rear. Look into the chamber and make sure any cartridge has been extracted and ejected, and that the chamber is empty. Leave the bolt open.
steps.prose: Bolt open, chamber empty, magazine out: that is the only state Vudoo calls safe, and the rifle stays in it for the whole clean.
steps.quote: 3. Open the bolt and check to ensure that the cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Unloading of the Rifle, item 3, Pg. 10

steps.title: Field strip complete: the book stops here
steps.action: That is as far as Vudoo's book takes the rifle apart: magazine out and bolt open. The book recommends taking the bolt out of the rifle for locking and storage, but it prints no procedure for removing it, so this guide does not either. Its cleaning section works on the breech face, receiver, crown, chamber, bore and bolt from here.
steps.prose: The book's feature diagram labels a side bolt release on the left of the receiver and says nothing more about it. For how to take the bolt out of your rifle, ask Vudoo's Service Department.
steps.quote: It is also recommended to completely remove the bolt from the firearm during locking and storage.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Locking Device Operation and Installation, item 3, Pg. 4

steps.title: Breech face first
steps.action: Look at the breech face with a flashlight. Light discolouration there is usually lead: pick it off with a plastic dental pick, because a brush will not usually shift it. Then brush the back of the breech face gently with a nylon armorer's brush.
steps.prose: Do this before the chamber and bore, as Vudoo orders it.
steps.quote: Perform this step before cleaning the chamber and the bore. Once you have removed any lead, clean the back of the breech face gently with the nylon armorers brush.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Care & Maintenance, Breech Face, Pg. 12
steps.warn: WARNING - LEAD EXPOSURE! SHOOTING OR CLEANING GUNS MAY EXPOSE YOU TO LEAD

steps.title: Brush round the inside of the receiver
steps.action: Run the nylon armorer's brush lightly round the inside of the receiver to dislodge any debris. A .223 chamber brush or a cheap bottle brush does the same job faster.
steps.quote: Using your nylon aromorers brush, run your brush round the inside of the receiver lightly to dislodge any foreign debris.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Care & Maintenance, Receiver, Pg. 12

steps.title: Brush the crown, nothing metal
steps.action: Put a little solvent on the brush and gently brush the crown at the muzzle to lift any carbon. Wipe the remaining film off with a dry rag.
steps.prose: The crown is where the bullet leaves the barrel, and a nick there costs accuracy.
steps.quote: Do not use any kind of metal device to scrape or poke at the crown of your barrel, as you may damage it.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Care & Maintenance, Crown of the Barrel, Pg. 12

steps.title: Chamber and bore: brush, then patches
steps.action: Wet the .22 caliber nylon bore brush with solvent and push it gently back and forth the full length of the bore two or three times. Then push one or two clean patches through on the jag. Repeat brush and patches until the patches come out clean.
steps.prose: Vudoo calls this the most critical part of the clean, because the chamber and bore decide a rimfire's accuracy. A dirty chamber also shows up as failures to feed or extract.
steps.quote: Now using your jag, push 1 or 2 clean patches through the bore.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Care & Maintenance, Chamber and Bore, Pg. 12

steps.title: Bolt body, bolt nose and extractors
steps.action: Scrub the bolt body and bolt nose with the nylon armorer's brush and a little solvent. Pull the extractors back lightly and brush the debris out from under them; a little compressed air helps clear what comes loose. Finish with light oil on the extractor pins and the cocking piece, and a little oil rubbed over the bolt body with your fingers.
steps.quote: Pull the extractors back lightly and brush any debris out from underneath them.
steps.cite: Vudoo Gun Works Owners Manual (V-22) — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Care & Maintenance, Bolt Body and Bolt Face, Pg. 12

deepAbsentReason: Vudoo Gun Works' V-22 owner's manual prints no disassembly procedure at all. Its Care & Maintenance section (Pg. 11-12) cleans the breech face, receiver, crown, chamber and bore, and the bolt body with the rifle as it is, then closes with a note that the barrel may need a few dozen rounds to re-season. It recommends removing the bolt for locking and storage (Pg. 4) without saying how. There is nothing deeper in the book, so this guide has no deep lane.

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE
tasks: Flashlight on the breech face: light discolouration there is usually lead
Lead picked off with a plastic dental pick; a brush will not usually remove it
Do this before the chamber and bore
Back of the breech face brushed gently with a nylon armorer's brush

cleaning.name: RECEIVER
tasks: Nylon armorer's brush run lightly round the inside of the receiver
A .223 chamber brush or a bottle brush also works

cleaning.name: CROWN
tasks: A little solvent on the brush, crown brushed gently to lift carbon
Remaining film wiped off with a dry rag
Never scrape or poke the crown with anything metal

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & BORE
tasks: Solvent-wet .22 caliber nylon bore brush, gently back and forth the full length of the bore 2-3 times
1 or 2 clean patches through on the jag
Brush and patches repeated until the patches come out clean
Going into storage: a lightly oiled patch down the bore last, against corrosion
A mild rimfire solvent is enough; .22 LR has no copper jacket to dissolve

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Bolt body and bolt nose scrubbed with the nylon armorer's brush and a little solvent
Extractors pulled back lightly, debris brushed out from under them
Compressed air to clear loose material
Light oil on the extractor pins and the cocking piece
A little oil rubbed over the bolt body with your fingers

reassembly: Vudoo's book prints no takedown, so nothing in this guide came apart and there is nothing to refit.
With the cleaning done and the chamber still empty, push the bolt forward and turn the handle down to close it.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle in a safe direction. Work the bolt as Vudoo describes it: raise the handle, draw the bolt to the rear to its stop, push it forward and turn the handle down. It should run and close without binding. Vudoo ends its unloading by closing the bolt and pressing the trigger to dry fire. After a full clean, expect to shoot a few dozen rounds before the barrel is fully re-seasoned.
